query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of 1 wt% TiC nanoparticles via powder metallurgy and hot isostatic pressing, followed by optimized processing conditions to ensure uniform distribution, will improve the strength-ductility balance, enhance high-temperature stability, and reduce creep and corrosion of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy.
generation.intervention: Introduction of 1 wt% TiC nanoparticles via powder metallurgy and hot isostatic pressing
generation.conditions: Sintering at 1000°C for 2 hours under 200 MPa, followed by aging at 600°C for 10 hours, and optimized processing conditions to ensure uniform distribution of TiC nanoparticles
generation.structural_mediator: Uniform dispersion of TiC nanoparticles along lamellar interfaces
generation.mechanism: Pinning of dislocations and grain boundaries by TiC nanoparticles, reducing creep strain and enhancing corrosion resistance through reduced defect density
generation.predicted_outcome: 25% increase in yield strength, 15% improvement in elongation, and a 30% reduction in creep rate at 500°C, along with enhanced corrosion resistance in saltwater environments
generation.boundary: Operating conditions: temperature range from -50°C to 500°C, stress range from 0 to 1000 MPa, and corrosion environments including saltwater and humid air
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in mechanical properties and corrosion resistance may vary depending on the uniformity of TiC nanoparticle distribution and the optimized processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and creep testing at 500°C, followed by corrosion testing in saltwater environments
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of TiC nanoparticles does not result in a significant improvement in yield strength, elongation, and creep rate, and does not enhance corrosion resistance, the hypothesis is falsified
